build: Pytxo CLI 2.0.2 as published on npm, run as `npx pytxo demo` with a warm npm cache. For the run, npm's global folder (npm_config_prefix) pointed at an empty directory, as on a machine with no global pytxo: this one has an older global install that a bare `npx pytxo` would otherwise run.

repo.name: pytxo demo (a pile of four branches)
repo.built: pytxo demo builds the files, branches and commits in a temporary directory, lands on that repository's main and deletes it afterwards

branches.claude/rename-price: renames price() to unitPrice() in src/cart.js

limits: The demo writes all four branches itself; no agent wrote them.
It shows the mechanism, not how often it happens in real projects.
The demo lands on the main of its own temporary repository and deletes it, so this record holds no receipt.
line_ms is the time each line of the first run reached a pipe, in ms from the start, so a test run's line shows when that run ended.
Timed on a laptop busy with other work, with a warm npm cache. A first run also downloads the package.
Six other timed runs of the same command on this laptop that day took 13.3 to 62.1 s, depending on what else it was doing.
